title: Cross-plan credit exchange and gracebanding for quota shortfalls
creator: Marin Patel
description: Deliver a controlled mechanism that allows unused credits from one paid plan/seat pool to be temporarily borrowed by another plan or route within the same organization when a quota shortfall would otherwise cause hard denials. The feature combines a configurable cross-plan credit exchange, tiered graceband windows (soft, transitional, hard), and prorated billing adjustments to ensure predictable economics and minimal customer disruption.
background: Customers on multi-product contracts frequently hit uneven usage spikes across routes or teams. Currently each entitlement is siloed and overages lead to immediate hard denials or unpredictable invoices. Sales and CS teams ask for a safe way to reduce interruptions (e.g., burst across entitlements) while preserving per-plan accounting. This initiative follows prior work on quota pooling and seeks to formalize exchange rules, UI surfaces, and billing acceptance criteria.
scope: In-scope: cross-plan credit borrowing within a single org for hosted API usage, adjustable graceband policy per plan, prorated invoice lines for exchanged credits, admin console controls to enable/disable exchanges, telemetry for reconciliation. Out-of-scope: cross-organization borrowing, Dedicated capacity autoscale policies, on-prem license transfers.
non_goals: Not implementing automatic invoice refunds for exchanges older than 90 days, not changing token pricing or base plan entitlements in this rollout, not enabling manual peer-to-peer credits between unrelated customers.
requirements: R1: Admin toggle at org-level to opt into cross-plan credit exchange
R2: Configurable graceband windows per plan: Soft (minutes), Transitional (hours), Hard (immediate denial if exhausted)
R3: Priority rules for borrowing: explicit allow list, then per-plan priority weights, then FIFO among eligible pools
R4: Exchange must surface a traceable ledger entry with source pool, target pool, amount, timestamp, and source of decision
R5: Billing must emit prorated invoice lines showing borrowed credits, effective rate, and reconciliation flags
R6: UI in Console to view active exchanges, historical ledger, and to manually revert an exchange within 24h
R7: Guardrails: daily cap on total borrowed credits per org and per-plan max borrow fraction
R8: Fail-open behavior: if billing reconciliation fails, exchanges remain but generate alerts and temporary invoice hold flag
R9: Audit logs emitted to customer SIEM (optional) when enabled via KMS/HSM integration
R10: Backfill and reconciliation: ability for billing job to reclassify usage and create adjusting invoice items within a 90-day window
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Org-level toggle operates: enabling exchange allows borrowing under configured rules; disabling prevents new borrows but does not auto-revert active exchanges
AC2: Soft graceband opens for a plan for a configurable window (e.g., 15 minutes) and returns HTTP 200 with 'charged-from-exchange' metadata in the response headers when borrowing occurs
AC3: Transitional window behavior throttles responses but allows reduced-rate serving (X% of normal throughput) consistent with policy
AC4: Hard denial occurs only after graceband windows and caps are exhausted and returns standard quota-exceeded error with clear error code and guidance link
AC5: Billing export contains distinct line items: 'Borrowed credits from {source_plan}', effective unit price, and correct prorated amount; invoice sample for test org matches expected values
AC6: Console displays active exchanges and a 90-day ledger; actions (revert within 24h) are enabled for org-admins and logged
AC7: Telemetry events emitted: credit_borrow_requested, credit_borrow_granted, credit_borrow_reverted, credit_borrow_settled (all include org_id, source_plan, target_plan, amount, request_id)
AC8: Reconciliation job can reconcile sample test data (1000 events) with zero unexplained balance after two runs
AC9: Guardrail caps prevent >25% of any source pool from being borrowed in acceptance tests and fire alerts when threshold approached
AC10: Documentation and customer-facing FAQ drafted and published in Console help center
billing_validation_steps: B1: Create test org with two plans: Plan A (100k tokens), Plan B (10k tokens), enable exchange
B2: Generate synthetic usage to exhaust Plan B and borrow 5k tokens from Plan A during soft window
B3: Run billing export and assert invoice contains 'Borrowed credits from Plan A' line, prorated price matches Plan B's rate where specified by policy
B4: Simulate reconciliation delay and confirm temporary invoice hold flag is set and cleared after job completes
B5: Revert an exchange within 24h and confirm billing adjustment line is created and ledger updated
B6: Run stress test with 10 concurrent borrow requests and validate priority rules and FIFO ordering
analytics_queries: Q1: Daily borrowed-credits-by-org: SELECT sum(amount) GROUP BY org_id WHERE event='credit_borrow_granted'
Q2: Borrow-failure-rate: percentage of credit_borrow_requested that were denied due to caps/graceband exhaustion
Q3: Median time-to-reconcile: track time between credit_borrow_granted and credit_borrow_settled
Q4: Revenue-impact projection: sum(prorated_amount) grouped by billing-cycle for test cohorts
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Beta): opt-in for 50 existing customers with and without enterprise contracts; monitor errors and reconciliation for 4 weeks
Phase 2 (Limited GA): open to all org-admins on hosted plans with guardrails enabled; surface billing sample in Console
Phase 3 (GA): enable default for new orgs with clear documentation and SDK header changes to include borrow metadata
Rollback: admin toggle off prevents new borrows and triggers a review run to clear transient states; billing team will issue manual adjustments if needed
risks: R1: Accounting complexity may create disputed invoices leading to CS escalation
R2: Latency impact when ledger writes are synchronous; design should prefer async but durable writes
R3: Behavioral complexity for customers may increase support volume; require clear UI/UX and docs
R4: Edge cases where multiple concurrent reconciliations create double-billing — mitigation: idempotent settlement with request_id
open_questions: Q1: Should borrowed credits always charge at target plan's unit price, or allow source-plan price as a premium? Decision needed for consistent accounting.
Q2: What default guardrail thresholds should we ship with (suggested: 10% per day, 25% absolute cap)?
Q3: For orgs with contractual enterprise discounts, how are discounts applied when borrowing across plans?
Q4: Should exchanges be visible in the API usage response body or only via headers/console ledger?
decisions: D1: Initial rollout will charge borrowed tokens at the target plan's effective unit price and include a 'borrow fee' metadata flag for later analysis
D2: Default guardrails: 10% daily borrow cap per org, 25% per-source-pool absolute cap; configurable by enterprise contract
D3: Exchanges will emit headers (X-Redwood-Borrowed: true) and include ledger_id in response headers for traceability
